decisions.decision: Buffer incoming documents through a durable queue
decisions.context: The system classifies millions of incoming documents per day, and volume varies strongly over the year. A durable buffer separates intake from classification capacity.
decisions.rationale: A queue buffers seasonal peaks and lets classification capacity scale independently of intake.

decisions.decision: Scale LLM classification workers with queue demand
decisions.context: Daily volume is large and seasonally variable. Worker capacity needs to follow the backlog while using an LLM-based classifier.
decisions.rationale: Autoscaling can raise throughput during seasonal peaks and reduce excess capacity when demand falls.
consequences: Capacity signals and scaling limits need configuration.
LLM service limits constrain peak throughput.

decisions.decision: Publish classification results through a shared result store and interface
decisions.context: Several teams consume the classifier's results. A common publication path gives consumers a consistent way to retrieve them.
decisions.rationale: A shared interface serves multiple teams without requiring the classifier to maintain a separate integration for each.
consequences: The interface needs a stable result schema.

decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. The system therefore needs ongoing quality monitoring with an operator-visible signal.
decisions.rationale: A dashboard gives operators a recurring view of quality changes and makes drift easier to spot than periodic review alone.
consequences: Quality indicators and thresholds need definition.
Dashboard alerts require an operational owner.
